annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Justice, Republic of Rwanda (with UNESCO, GIZ, EU)
key_provisions_or_claims: Two-day training on 14-15 April for 31 Rwandan judicial operators on AI, data protection and rule of law
Based on UNESCO's Global Toolkit on AI and the Rule of Law
Highlights AI risks: bias, discrimination, black boxes, lack of accountability and transparency
Speakers call for clear legal frameworks and ethical guidelines grounded in data protection
Notes Rwanda's National AI Policy as a starting point
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Global Toolkit on AI and the Rule of Law
annotation.summary_en: Rwandan Ministry of Justice news item on a two-day UNESCO/GIZ/EU-supported training for 31 judicial operators on AI, data protection and the rule of law, based on UNESCO's Global Toolkit. It stresses AI's benefits and risks (bias, opacity, accountability) and the need for legal frameworks and ethical guidelines.
annotation.title_clean: AI, Data Protection and the Rule of Law
